record.paper_title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
record.original_question: Temporal contact networks can exhibit coordinated bursts of contacts, such as many individuals temporarily gathering at the same place and time. How do such coordinated bursts affect disease spread and the epidemic threshold on temporal networks?

evidence.quote: In real-world social interactions, it is possible to observe coordinated bursts of contacts.
For example, wildlife may gather at a common water source during a draught, temporarily placing them in close contact. To date, the effects of this phenomenon remain unexplored.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a temporal contact network represented as a sequence of time-stamped contacts (i,j,t) among a population of N individuals, where each contact denotes a potentially infectious interaction at time t. On such a network, run a standard compartmental spreading process (e.g., SIS or SIR) in which an infectious individual transmits along each contact independently with per-contact probability β (or rate β) and recovers at rate μ. The epidemic threshold is the critical value of β/μ above which a macroscopic outbreak occurs in the limit of large N.

Now suppose the temporal network exhibits coordinated bursts of contacts: at certain random times t_k, a large subset S_k ⊂ {1,…,N} of individuals becomes simultaneously and pairwise (or densely) in contact for a short duration Δ_k, after which contacts revert to a baseline temporal pattern. The sizes |S_k|, durations Δ_k, inter-burst intervals, and memberships may follow prescribed distributions, and these synchronized burst events are correlated across individuals (in contrast to independent per-edge burstiness).

Determine, analytically or through a tractable model, how such coordinated bursts modify (i) the epidemic threshold and (ii) the size and time course of the resulting outbreak, compared with a baseline temporal network having the same marginal contact rates but without coordinated bursts. In particular, characterize the dependence of the threshold shift on the burst-size distribution, burst frequency, and burst duration.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface work on burstiness in temporal networks (e.g., burstiness-controlled cascades, bursty communication patterns) and reviews of temporal-network epidemic thresholds, but no work specifically modeling the effect of coordinated/synchronized bursts of contacts on the epidemic threshold was found. The phenomenon was explicitly described as unexplored in the review that posed the question, and subsequent literature appears to have treated burstiness primarily at the level of individual edges or nodes rather than coordinated group bursts.

status_evidence.title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: To date, the effects of [coordinated bursts of contacts] remain unexplored.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in the review.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of cascades on burstiness-controlled temporal networks
status_evidence.snippet: Studies burstiness as an edge-level property controlling cascade dynamics, not coordinated group bursts.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses edge-burstiness, not coordinated synchronized bursts.

status_evidence.title: Concurrency measures in the era of temporal network epidemiology: a review
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews concurrency and temporal-network epidemic measures without dedicated treatment of coordinated burst events.
status_evidence.claim: Recent reviews do not report a resolution of the coordinated-bursts question.
